dollar_base: 2025 real dollars; primary benefit indexing starts in 2030

basis.scenarios: Analyst stress tests, not estimated take-up probabilities or forecast percentiles. Coverage is a conditional eligible-family share, never imputed SSN/ITIN status.
basis.ctc: FAM-1A amounts and 2021 increase phaseouts; unselected indexing anchor, age-17 layer and ODC allocation are branched. Incremental-receipt convention preserves source credits.
basis.care: FAM-2A income tiers and deduction arithmetic; source paid care identifies monetary exposure. Pre-K expense share and usable access are assumptions.
basis.smi: State weighted median cash income of four-person CPS SPM units (>=30 observations); otherwise national fallback, adjusted sqrt(family size/4). Proxy, not official administrative SMI.
basis.food: Observed modal free-lunch SPM value among low-income school-age units; net of current school/summer values. Breakfast excluded from SPM. $60 Summer EBT policy through three assumed months and existing 185%-FPG eligibility proxy.
basis.housing: 100,000 additional awards in 2030, 400,000 in 2034 across all proxy-eligible renter households; random-allocation outcome mixture, lease-up separate. State median proxy is not HUD AMI or an observed waitlist.
basis.leave: FAM-3A employee contribution included as cost-side stress; leave benefits not imputed. Employer incidence separate.
basis.carbon: Optional reduced-form extension from the existing carbon model, both adult dividend and consumer cost included. Not part of focused child-policy headline.
basis.health: Optional proportional reduction in actual SPM MOOP; uncalibrated sensitivity, not a health-policy score.
basis.emergency: Primary $0 cash credit because HOU-1 cash/construction split is unsized. Optional bounded research cash scenario expires after 2031.
basis.baseline: Source-year net resources held in 2025 purchasing power; +/-5% of each threshold is a resource adequacy stress, not an economic forecast.
basis.population: Optional CBO age/sex growth ratios anchored to CPS; not absolute Social Security-area population controls.
